note: ep08 Short 'Pay It Off or Invest?' (2026-10-30), 9:16, published with the long-form. The same $400,000 loan and $800 a month replayed at the same rate from two real starts: June 1993, then September 1972. Top half A = pays down, bottom half B = invests. `year` = years since signing. Numbers checked by tools/validate-ep08-story.mjs (short section) and asserted by render/short-ep08-nguyens.html.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: An extra eight hundred a month: pay off the mortgage, or invest it? Same rate, about seven point four percent, two real starts. *Who ends up richer?*

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two thousand. Stocks are flying. *A hundred twenty-six thousand* invested.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two thousand nine. My house is paid off.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two crashes later: the same *hundred twenty-six thousand*. And I still owe a hundred ninety-four.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Twenty twenty-three. Paying down wins, by about *thirty-six thousand*.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Now the same rate, in nineteen seventy-two.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nineteen seventy-four. A crash. I've got *eleven thousand*.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nineteen eighty-eight. My house is paid off.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Two thousand two. Investing wins, by about *three hundred twenty thousand*.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Every start since eighteen seventy-one, at seven percent: investing won about seven in ten. At five percent or below, every time. At eight, less than half. *Your rate decides.* Full story on the channel.
